Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the final innings of this test match! The umpires are out in the middle and the West Indian skipper, Kraigg Brathwaite is joined by Mikyle Louis to open for the hosts. Temba Bavuma has decided to start straight away with Keshav Maharaj. Here we go!
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

The West Indies have a challenging 20-minute period before Lunch ahead as they start their innings. With 72 overs remaining in the day, the dark clouds gathering in the distance suggest that there might be interruptions, potentially affecting the amount of play. A wicket or two before Lunch will put the cat amongst the pigeons in the Windies' camp. It is all set up for an exciting conclusion to this Test. Back in a bit for the start of the fourth inning.

Aiden Markram fell on 38, but Tristan Stubbs continued to capitalize on the opportunity. Having been dropped on 31, Stubbs showcased his range and power, shifting gears to a T20-like approach. His aggressive play paid off as he reached his maiden Test century, significantly boosting South Africa’s total. The ball that dismissed Tristan Stubbs kept low, an encouraging sign for South Africa who will come out aggressively with the ball, looking to exploit any assistance from the pitch.

South Africa are happy with what they have they got on the board and have decided to DECLARE! Starting the day at 30/0, South Africa added 143 runs in 24 overs to finish with 173 on the board, setting the West Indies a target of 298 runs. Tony de Zorzi and Aiden Markram picked up where they left off on Day 4, showing intent from the outset. The West Indies managed to gain some control with the introduction of Jason Holder, who kept things tight. Jomel Warrican made an immediate impact, dismissing De Zorzi with a leg-side strangle just before the end of the first hour. However, with Tristan Stubbs arriving at the crease and the second hour beginning, there was a noticeable shift in gears from South Africa.

OUT! TIMBER! Kemar Roach follows back with a good delivery that keeps low! South Africa declare the innings at 173/3 setting a target of 298 runs for the hosts! Kemar Roach hits the deck hard, on a good length, angling in on middle and off. Tristan Stubbs plays across the line hoping for the ball to bounce but it stays low and scoots under his bat to rattle the stumps. Tristan Stubbs ends his scintillating innings at 68(50).

Commentary.Commentary: We are ready to begin the final day of this first Test match under the clear skies of Port of Spain. The two umpires make their way to the centre, closely followed by the West Indies players, who spread out across the field. Meanwhile, the South African openers, Aiden Markram and Tony de Zorzi, stride out to resume their innings at the crease. Kemar Roach is handed the ball and will start the proceedings for West Indies! Away we go..

PITCH REPORT - Nikhil Uttamchandani and Stacy-Ann King are near the deck. Nikhil begins by noting that, unlike typical Day 5 surfaces, this one shows minimal wear and tear, largely because only 214 overs have been bowled so far. He mentions that it's currently bright with clear skies, though rain showers are expected later in the day. Stacy has a close look at the deck and observes that the cracks are starting to open up, but she reckons they won't come into play. She feels that batting will get easier, and it will be important for the bowlers to remain patient.

Lungi Ngidi is in for a flash interview. He says that the game is in a good position for them but it's very unfortunate with the weather, however, them bowling out West Indies once in 91 odd overs has given them the idea of how to go ahead with things. Further says that the ball is in their court this morning and they will need to make the most of it.

Kemar Roach is in for a chat. He says that the first hour is crucial for them. Lauds Jayden Seales for the way he has bowled and says that he is proud of what Seales has achieved so far in his career. Feels that Seales did well in England and it is about how he channels his aggression into performances for West Indies.
GREAT VISUALS! The sun is shining brightly, and the players are out on the field, indulging in their warm-up drills. We're all set for a prompt start to the day. Stick around for the action!

On the other hand, West Indies will likely have a draw in the back of their minds, but they should also focus on putting up a strong fight and attempting to turn the game around. They will need to put the disappointments of Day 4 behind them and come out with renewed determination, aiming to execute their plans with sharper fielding and more disciplined bowling if they are to have any chance on this final day. The weather, although not entirely promising, is expected to be an improvement over yesterday, which is a positive sign given how much the game shifted in just those two hours of play. We're hopeful for a timely start today. Stay with us as we bring you all the updates and action from Port of Spain on this decisive Day 5!

South Africa made the most of the limited play that rain permitted on Day 4 and will be eager to seize control as they head into the final day, comfortably placed in the driving seat with a lead of 154 runs and all 10 wickets in hand. The bowlers were exceptional in the first hour and a half of play on Day 4, tearing through six wickets of the West Indies, setting the stage for the Proteas to dominate with the bat in the final 20 minutes. This commanding position has put them well ahead in the match. If the weather allows for a full day of play, the Proteas are certain to come out all guns blazing, aiming to set a formidable target that they will be confident in defending, especially given how the pitch has deteriorated, a factor that could play into the hands of their bowlers, led by the ever-reliable Keshav Maharaj.

Hello and a warm welcome to the final day of this captivating first Test between the West Indies and South Africa at the Queen's Park Oval in Port of Spain. With the match finely poised, all eyes are on the weather, which could play a decisive role in determining the outcome. Despite the uncertainty, we remain hopeful and optimistic for a significant amount of play on this crucial Day 5, which holds the potential to deliver a result beyond just a draw.
... DAY 5, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, despite the rain delays and interruptions, this Test match has moved along briskly and now promises a thrilling conclusion, provided the weather cooperates. The forecast for Day 5 isn’t very promising, but hope persists. It will be yet another early start with the first ball on Day 5 to be bowled at 7 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT), weather permitting. As always, you can join us earlier for the build-up. See you then. Cheers!

The captain of South Africa, Temba Bavuma is in for a chat. He says that due to the delay caused by the inclement weather, it was important for them to stay in the right frame of mind. Lauds Keshav Maharaj for the way he bowled. On the thinking behind starting with Aiden Markram with the second new ball, he says that he wanted to see how the bounce was with the red cherry. Mentions that the cracks have started to open up, which is a good sign for them in the fourth innings. Hopes that they can get a full day's play to have a realistic chance. Feels that they need to take care of the first hour and take it from there.

With South Africa firmly in control, the final day of this first Test match hinges on just two factors, the weather and time. If conditions allow, the Proteas will aim to start aggressively, scoring quickly in the opening session to set a formidable target. Their goal will then be to dismiss the West Indies with half a day in hand, securing a decisive victory. For the West Indies, the disappointing end to Day 4 must be swiftly overcome. They will need to respond with resilience, making the most of any aggressive batting from South Africa and not letting them get to where they want to be.

In response, Aiden Markram and Tony de Zorzi came out with intent, adding 30 quick runs in just 20 minutes, pushing the lead to 154. Kraigg Brathwaite turned to Jayden Seales for the last over, but the day ended on a sour note for the hosts, as a dropped catch by Kavem Hodge in the final over epitomized their struggles on Day 4.

When the second new ball was introduced, Kagiso Rabada wasted no time in making an impact, ripping through the West Indian tail. Despite a valiant effort from Jomel Warrican, who remained unbeaten with a spirited 35 off 32 balls, the West Indies were eventually bowled out for 233, conceding a substantial 124-run lead to South Africa.

The day began cautiously for the West Indies, with Jason Holder and Kavem Hodge navigating the early pressure applied by Aiden Markram and Keshav Maharaj. Maharaj was particularly threatening, forcing Holder to take on Markram while carefully negotiating Maharaj's probing deliveries. However, Markram had the final say, delivering a stunning ball that uprooted Holder's off-stump, sparking a dramatic collapse. Maharaj quickly followed up, dismissing Joshua Da Silva, which further deepened the hosts' troubles.

After losing a couple of sessions to rain and enduring a gruelling six-hour wait for the much-anticipated resumption of play, we were finally rewarded with a riveting couple of hours of cricket. The West Indies were dismissed for 233 runs, and the South African openers, Aiden Markram and Tony de Zorzi, seized the opportunity, confidently punishing every loose delivery. Their solid defence and aggressive stroke play have propelled South Africa to a commanding lead of 154 runs. With the momentum firmly in their favour, South Africa will be buoyed by their performance, eagerly anticipating clear skies on Day 5 to capitalize on their advantage and push for victory.
